targetText: Socialists have always condemned war between nations as barbarous and brutal. But our attitude towards war is fundamentally different from that of the bourgeois pacifists (supporters and advocates of peace) and of the Anarchists.
summary: Lenin draws a sharp distinction between Marxist scientific analysis of war and bourgeois pacifism or anarchism, noting that socialists oppose wars of imperialist plunder while supporting progressive wars of national liberation and class emancipation.

targetText: "War is the Continuation of Politics by Other" (i.e., Violent) "Means"
summary: Lenin invokes Clausewitz's famous formula to demonstrate that World War I was not an accidental or purely defensive catastrophe, but the inevitable violent continuation of decades of imperialist rivalries for colonies and markets.

targetText: Social-chauvinism is advocacy of the idea of "defence of the fatherland" in the present war.
summary: Lenin defines social-chauvinism as socialism in words and chauvinism in deeds: defending the reactionary fatherland in an imperialist robbery war and sabotaging the proletarian class struggle.
context: Leaders like Karl Kautsky in Germany and Georgi Plekhanov in Russia justified supporting their own nations in World War I under slogans of national defense.

targetText: A revolutionary class cannot but wish for the defeat of its government in a reactionary war, cannot fail to see that its military reverses facilitate its overthrow.
summary: Lenin formulates the foundational principle of revolutionary defeatism, holding that workers must actively seek the defeat of their own imperialist ruling class to accelerate the collapse of the capitalist regime.
